summary: The island network: an authored node/tether graph, reachability that changes with tether state, and a trigger condition and effect that read and change it

coordination.notes: docs/BUILD_OUT_PLAN.md item 1, first slice. content/world/island_network.prototype.json declared six nodes and eight tethers since the design authority landed; nothing had ever read it. Adopted verbatim as the main pack's rules.islandNetwork -- an optional rule, not one of the four schema-version-1 reserved keys, so no other lane's assumptions about resources/items/triggers/quests move. Nodes are pure membership (roles are descriptive, unread, same treatment as the record's own topology/knowledgePolicy per the campaign-clock precedent). A tether is traversable when its *effective* state -- an authored default, overridable by FactionWorld.tether_overrides play state -- is open or conditional; blocked, hidden and corrupted are not. network_reachable is a real breadth-first search honouring one-way tethers. Two new closed trigger clauses, NetworkReachable (condition) and SetTetherState (effect, refusing an undeclared tether and a no-op), let the already-shipped trigger contract read and change the graph: the concrete form of 'tether state changing reachability without moving geography.' Explicitly NOT in this slice, and recorded as such rather than implied finished: faction dispatch and player movement still route through from_scenario's invented runtime destinations (preview.<faction>.holding, island.contested_clearing), not through these named nodes, and no walkable cell is assigned to any node's region. Weather (the next contract) needs only the graph and its reachability to move fronts along tethers, which this slice provides in full.
